objective: Provide password confirmation at signup and Cognito verification-code recovery for email-verified accounts, with an Account details entry point and a static email-verification disclaimer.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: USERS-006 and USERS-007 are merged and deployed. A separate human-reviewed Director prerequisite grants the backend role pool-scoped cognito-idp:AdminUserGlobalSignOut permission. Cognito AdminGetUser is already present and scoped. No AWS write is part of this task.

Start gate: a Director-owned policy/scope PR has made the specific backend/alembic/versions/** migration path writable to the code agent and merged before this task starts. The task worker does not change .ai/policy.json.

The sign-in page retains an accessible Forgot password link below the password field. The request page contains a labelled email input, a confirm button, and a static disclaimer that users must verify their email before resetting their password. The code-entry page has labelled code, New password, and Confirm password inputs.

For every syntactically valid request, known, unknown, disabled, and unverified addresses receive the same success status, body, and user-facing message, with no account-existence, verification, or delivery detail. Only an email-verified account can receive a recovery code, delivered by Cognito's existing default email sender to its verified_email recovery method. Unverified accounts receive no code. The app does not rely on SES or a custom sender for recovery. Reset does not set email_verified.
Requests are rate-limited by normalized account address and source IP to at most 5 requests per hour per key. Unknown, disabled, and unverified-account cases do not reveal which case occurred.

Recovery uses Cognito ForgotPassword and ConfirmForgotPassword verification-code operations only. Cognito owns code expiry, single-use, and attempt controls. The app does not create custom reset links or app-issued reset tokens, persist or log recovery codes, or maintain reset-token records.

The backend owns successful code confirmation so it can persist the valid-after barrier and perform global sign-out. Cognito enforces the configured password policy; the application never stores or logs a plaintext current password.

New password and confirmation must match before submission. A mismatch is an accessible field error and makes no Cognito confirmation call. Cognito rejects invalid, expired, consumed, or exhausted codes without changing the password; the app does not expose account details.

The sign-up form has labelled Password and Confirm password fields. A mismatch is an accessible field error and makes no Cognito SignUp request; matching values submit once. Optional email verification behavior remains unchanged.

If the signed-in user navigates to the password-recovery route, the app signs them out and clears the active session before exposing a form that can submit a recovery request or password change. A test proves that no recovery request is sent before sign-out completes.

Account settings begins with an Account details section. It shows the signed-in user's email in an Email row and a Password row with a Reset password button instead of a password value. The button opens the same password-recovery route used from sign-in.

Before calling Cognito ConfirmForgotPassword, the backend durably writes a restrictive pending valid-after cutoff keyed by the resolved Cognito subject, independent of whether a local profile row exists. Every locally JWT-validated API request treats a pending cutoff as active and rejects verified ID tokens whose auth_time is at or before it; barrier lookup fails closed. Choose the cutoff to account for Cognito auth_time's one-second precision so pre-reset tokens cannot pass, and document any brief reauthentication delay caused by rounding. This write must succeed before code confirmation is attempted.

If Cognito definitively rejects a code as invalid or expired, and therefore did not change the password, the backend may remove only that attempt's pending cutoff, without deleting or moving back any previously committed cutoff. If cleanup fails, leave the pending cutoff active and fail closed. For timeouts, transport errors, or any result that does not prove the password was unchanged, leave the pending cutoff active; do not roll it back. A pending cutoff left by an interrupted attempt may deny old sessions, but a normal sign-in after that cutoff is allowed. Rate limiting applies before recovery attempts.

After Cognito confirms the code, the backend commits the pending cutoff as the durable valid-after barrier, then calls Cognito AdminUserGlobalSignOut to stop refresh-token sessions and requires normal sign-in. It sends no separate post-reset password-changed email and does not automatically create an authenticated session. A successful reset is not reported until code confirmation, durable barrier commit, and global sign-out have succeeded. If barrier commit or global sign-out fails after confirmation, retain the restrictive cutoff; never restore the prior cutoff.

Tests cover known/unknown/disabled/unverified response equivalence, verified code recovery and no delivery for unverified accounts, rate limits, signup and reset password mismatch, no Cognito signup or code confirmation on mismatch, sign-out before recovery submission, Account details and its shared route, pending and committed cutoff rejection of pre-reset ID tokens on locally JWT-validated API requests (including a Cognito subject without a profile), cutoff persistence before Cognito confirmation, cleanup after definite invalid/expired-code rejection without deleting an earlier cutoff, retention after ambiguous confirmation errors and post-confirmation failures, failure-closed barrier lookup, global sign-out, and no email_verified mutation. Local browser rows use localhost and a human-controlled dev-pool address; report evidence or NOT DONE for signup mismatch and success, verified code recovery, unverified generic response/no delivery and disclaimer, reset mismatch, and Account settings entry.
No new dependency. The relevant Users and Frontend module references record the flow and its security boundary.
